dedupe_keys.name: sup3rload hourly us electricity load under electrification and climate scenarios

description: Sup3rLoad is a data set of hourly electricity load for the contiguous United States that varies jointly with electrification and weather. It was produced by Ryan Jones, Grant Buster, Ben Haley, Caitlin Murphy and Margaret Torn at Evolved Energy Research, the National Laboratory of the Rockies and UC Berkeley, sponsored by the DOE Grid Deployment Office. It spans two electrification scenarios, five CMIP6 Earth system models downscaled through Sup3rCC under SSP2-4.5, six scenario years from 2025 to 2050, sixty weather years from 2000 to 2059 and fourteen end-use subsectors. Profiles for weather-sensitive subsectors (heating, cooling, light-duty electric vehicle charging and data centre cooling) come from neural network regressions trained on building energy simulations, applied to downscaled weather and combined in a stock-turnover demand model calibrated to state electricity sales and hourly system loads. Coverage is 48 states and the District of Columbia at hourly resolution. Data are one downloadable NetCDF file in NetCDF4 format on the Open Energy Data Initiative (last updated September 2026) under the site's Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 terms at no cost. Caveats: loads are modelled projections, and one emissions pathway is used. Simulation uses are resource adequacy, capacity planning and climate stress testing of power systems.
